findings: The minimum coefficient valuation exists because valuations are integral and bounded below. The least index attaining it exists, and the finitely many earlier terms admit the stated positive epsilon.

For fixed z of positive valuation less than epsilon, every later term has valuation at least mu+(d+1)v(z), while the finitely many earlier terms have strictly larger valuation than the dth term. The convergent tail therefore cannot cancel it.
The cyclotomic polynomial (1+t)^(2^(n-1))+1 is Eisenstein including n=1. Its roots have valuation 1/2^(n-1); only finitely many n remain outside the zero-free punctured annulus.

Evaluation is defined for bounded-denominator series at positive-valuation parameters. An annihilator evaluates to an invertible scalar at all other characters, forcing the specialized module element to vanish. This does not require a cohomology base-change isomorphism.
